Sports.title: 'Some people prefer Manchester or London... but I love Burnley': How $100m NFL star JJ Watt has embraced his role as Clarets co-owner - and even designed their new shirt
Sports.content:
'Some people prefer Manchester or London... but I love Burnley': How $100m NFL star JJ Watt has embraced his role as Clarets co-owner - and even designed their new shirt

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

JJ Watt wants to restore the Burnley of old. For a man used to the glitzy environs of America's NFL, who once had a $100million contract and lived in a place called Paradise Valley, he comes across remarkably in touch with this humble corner of Lancashire which he claims to love.

'For a very long time, you knew what you were getting at Burnley,' the club's minority owner tells Daily Mail Sport. 'You were in for a fight.

'I want a strong identity. We are going to outwork everybody, we are going to out-tough everybody. You are in for a very long day.'

If this all sounds rather Sean Dyche-coded, you'd be right. Burnley lacked their usual grit last season. The Clarets are back in the Championship after an abysmal relegation – their fifth divisional change in as many seasons. They won one of their last 29 games and had the league's worst defensive record. Pride in the shirt feels at a low ebb and, as such, Watt has made a change.

Burnley have released a new away kit, designed by Watt over the course of two years, which harks back to the club's history and resurrects an old crest. He spent time filming the promo on a nearby dairy farm and driving a milk cart over Lancastrian potholes. For a man who repeats the word 'work' 10 times during our interview, it feels fitting.

'The history and tradition of the club is what makes it special,' says Watt. 'Maybe some people prefer London or Manchester, but going around Burnley, I love it.

Burnley co-owner JJ Watt is hoping they can fight their way out of the Championship again

The Clarets are aiming to be promoted from the second tier for a third consecutive time

'We’re trying to really capture the essence of what Burnley is. The reason I built this kit is to try and preserve that history.'

It will take more than a polyester jersey and sweet talk to dispel the gloom from Turf Moor. They last won at home 286 days ago, when England had only just qualified for the World Cup.

First-team stars in Jaidon Anthony and Maxime Esteve have left, while Lesley Ugochukwu has gone on loan to Galatasaray. Scott Parker was sacked in April and the Clarets have appointed Nicky Hayen, who won the Belgian Pro League with Club Brugge in 2023-24, as his successor. It is a gamble.

'One of the first things Nicky said when he came in was that we need to train twice a day,' says Watt, a former Pizza Hut delivery man. 'I absolutely love that. It’s all about his work ethic, his tactics, his aggressiveness. We always want to be on the front foot.

'He wants these guys to have no egos, to put the crest before their last name, and it’s been great so far.'

'Great' is perhaps a stretch – Burnley are winless in five pre-season games against Cincinnati, Columbus Crew, Real Salt Lake, Ajax, and sister club Espanyol, though Hayen took a watching brief for the first two.

Watt wants to add his expertise without being overbearing. He and Hayen will discuss tactics, set-pieces and how to optimise a player's diet and recovery.

They have already gone about reinforcing the midfield, making Florentino's loan from Benfica permanent for £20.8million, and bringing in Ugo Raghouber from Lille.

The former NFL star models their new away kit, which harkens back to the club's history

He relies on the support of his wife Kealia, a former United States international player

Former Club Brugge manager Nicky Hayen - who won them a league title - has taken the reins

Watt has been involved with Burnley for three years and his arrival was treated with some scepticism. When 12 of the Premier League's 20 clubs have American owners, the last thing many traditional English fans want is another new face from across the pond with their bombast and unusual sporting ideas – though some years, Burnley fans probably wouldn't mind scrapping relegation.

To his credit, Watt is a long-time follower of football and speaks with authenticity. He played as a kid, watched matches at the crack of dawn as an NFL player, and his wife, Kealia, is a former United States international. Crucially, during our chat at least, he calls the sport by its correct name.

'I was drawn to the English game because of the passion, the history, and traditions,' he says.

'My favourite custom by far is my matchday routine where I get dropped off at the Royal Dyche and have a pint of Guinness with everybody there.

'Then I take a little walk around the corner to Burnley Miners' Club where I get myself one Bene Bomb. Then I walk the rest of the way into the Bob Lord Stand and get myself ready for the match. I meet supporters and hear the pulse of what they’re thinking.'

He can't always be in England for matches, but watches from Houston. Burnley are gathering popularity Stateside, where they spent some of pre-season.

‘It’s pretty funny how matchday has grown. My phone used to be silent on matchdays when we won or scored,' he explains.

'I’d text somebody and say, “hey, we just won,” and they’d say, “I didn’t know it was on.” Now, my phone is blowing up the second we score. My dad is texting me, I’ve got random people coming out of the woodwork. I’ll know if my TV is lagging or not because I’ll have everybody texting me when I haven’t seen a goal yet.

'It’s been really cool to see so many Burnley fans, random kids on the streets wearing old Burnley kits.’

Whether they'll come to treasure the new away strip will depend partly on the memories they make in it. Promotion is the target. As ever, the Championship remains an unpredictable beast.

Sports.title: Arsene Wenger has ruined his own legacy. We once thought he was The Professor, now we see the truth - a silent stooge following his master Gianni Infantino... and is ex-Arsenal boss the real brains behind FIFA's hated schemes?
Sports.content:
Speaking in February on the tenth anniversary of Gianni Infantino’s accession as FIFA president, Arsene Wenger paid tribute to his friend for overseeing a ‘huge improvement’ in world football.

‘Gianni is always ready to move forward and to create new ideas. He’s open to new ideas,’ said Wenger.

Say what you want about Infantino, he’s most definitely open to ideas.

The idea to have a World Cup in Qatar at Christmas time, and increase the number of teams at the tournament this summer to 48. If he gets his way, it will be 64 in four years’ time, when the tournament is already being played across six countries.

The idea to introduce mandatory hydration breaks at the World Cup this summer, thinking we wouldn’t see them for the commercial grab they really were, and to have the finalists from Spain and Argentina kicking their heels in the dressing room at half-time for the best part of half an hour waiting for Madonna and Co to get off the pitch at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

It was Infantino’s idea to award President Donald Trump the ridiculous FIFA Peace Prize, and then say nothing when the Iran team were banished to train in Mexico while Trump's war against them raged in the Middle East, or when the Somalian referee Omar Artan was denied entry to the US.

‘Gianni Infantino is always ready to move forward and to create new ideas. He’s open to new ideas,’ said Arsene Wenger

Say what you want about Infantino, he’s most definitely open to ideas

And it’s his preposterous idea to carve up the World Cup and sell it to private investors for £3.1billion by strong-arming FIFA’s 211 member associations into accepting his proposals, thus plunging world football into crisis.

All the while, Wenger has hovered at Infantino’s right hand like a silent stooge, a sight we witnessed so often in North America this summer.

As FIFA’s chief of global football development, the 76-year-old Frenchman is part of Infantino’s inner circle. One of the people, it’s fair to assume, who would have been aware of the great World Cup sell-off when so many other executives weren’t. For all we know, Wenger may have played an active role in hatching the plot given that he has Infantino’s ear.

Either way, it’s not a good look for the man English football first came to know 30 years ago when he arrived from Japan to take over as Arsenal manager.

The Professor, they called him. The forward-thinking coach whose ideas had a profound effect on the Arsenal culture and beyond the marbled halls of Highbury.

Wenger has continued to influence football’s development since he was appointed by Infantino in November 2019, 18 months after he had left Arsenal after 22 years in charge.

Among other things, he heads up the £160million FIFA Talent Coach Programme which develops young players in poorer countries where the path to professional football is lacking, and for that he deserves credit. He also leads a FIFA taskforce on player welfare which aims to address concerns over the increasing demands of the football calendar, although how Wenger’s proposal to stage the World Cup every two years would help in that regard is anyone’s guess.

It would be refreshing to think that a man of his influence and intelligence would be able to stand up to Infantino’s rampant egotism, but sadly that doesn’t seem to be the case.

It’s not a good look for the man English football first came to know 30 years ago when he arrived from Japan to take over as Arsenal manager and turned them into champions

Wenger will do what he always does these days. He will follow his master and nod along to whatever hare-brained idea Infantino comes up with next

Before the World Cup final, he claimed the new 48-team format had been a success – though at least had the decency to admit that not everyone was a fan of the hydration breaks.

It would be fascinating to hear what Wenger really thinks of the plan to sell off the World Cup and Infantino’s offer to give member associations £30million if they accept it by September 19, which has met with such resistance around the globe including the threat of a UEFA boycott. But let’s not hold our breath. He will do what he always does these days. He will follow his master and nod along to whatever hare-brained idea Infantino comes up with next.

FIFA tried to extinguish the fire on Friday as its president faced growing calls to step down. ‘Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain,’ read a statement.

But they aren’t fooling anyone. The world can see Infantino for what he is now – and we see Wenger standing squarely behind him.

Sports.title: Arsenal reach £77m agreement in principle to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle - as Premier League champions plan medical next week
Sports.content:
Arsenal have reached an agreement in principle to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle - and have set aside a day next week for the Brazil midfielder's medical.

It is understood that the fee agreed for the Newcastle captain is £77million plus add-ons.

The 28-year-old's contract has not yet been signed and finer details are to be sorted but Daily Mail Sport can confirm a deal is now very close.

The Magpies had been reluctant to part with their captain after losing other key players - such as Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon - this summer but the Premier League champions have gone all out to get the deal done.

Bruno Guimaraes is set to become the latest key Newcastle player to leave this summer

The Brazilian was part of the Newcastle side that won the club's first major trophy for 70 years - the Carabao Cup in March 2025

He is the third key player to leave Newcastle this summer, joining Anthony Gordon (second left) and Sandro Tonali (second right), while manager Eddie Howe has also left the club

As revealed by Daily Mail Sport, Guimaraes dropped a bombshell on the Newcastle hierarchy several weeks ago by informing them of his desire to leave. And he did not fly with the rest of the Toon squad to their pre-season training camp in La Manga on Friday.

The Magpies also saw manager Eddie Howe leave the club yesterday after four and a half years.

He would become Arsenal's fourth signing of the summer, after they made Piero Hincapie's loan deal from Bayer Leverkusen permanent, signed free agent former Leeds United goalkeeper Illan Meslier and struck a £36m deal for Club Brugge's Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

Arsenal first tried to sign Guimaraes in 2022 from Lyon, but Newcastle stole a march on the midfielder, who has won 48 caps for his country and played in this summer's World Cup.

Sports.title: Eddie Howe sends emotional message to Newcastle fans as club confirms bombshell exit - and labels his five-year spell at St James' Park a 'privilege of my lifetime'
Sports.content:
Eddie Howe has delivered an emotional farewell to Newcastle United supporters as the club confirmed his departure in a statement on Friday.

Howe, who established Newcastle as European regulars and won the 2025 Carabao Cup during his near five-year spell in charge at St James' Park, came to an agreement to leave his role with immediate effect this week after contemplating his future over the summer.

The Englishman informed Newcastle of his wish to leave earlier this month but agreed to stay on until a replacement was found, with German coach Matthias Jaissle now stepping in to succeed him ahead of the new 2026-27 season.

As part of a statement shared by the club to their website on Friday, Howe described the opportunity as a 'privilege of a lifetime'.

'After a period of personal reflection, I have decided that now is the right time for me to step away from my role as head coach of Newcastle United,' he confirmed.

'After nearly five years of giving my life, heart and soul into the club with unrelenting energy, I feel that it is in the best interests of both myself and the club to step away, recharge and take a break.

Eddie Howe delivered an emotional farewell statement to Newcastle United fans on Friday

'Although it's been incredibly difficult to make this decision, I know in my heart that it's the right one. I have always put the best interests of Newcastle before my own in every single decision I have made whilst I've been here and this one is no different.

'It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have been the manager of Newcastle United.

'It is difficult to put into words what this club, the city and its supporters mean, and will always mean, to me and my family. From the moment myself, Jason and all of the staff arrived nearly half a decade ago, Newcastle instantly felt like home and the people here welcomed us with open arms. We took huge pride in representing the club from day one and this city will always hold a very special place in our hearts.

'There have been so many incredible moments in our time here. From fighting relegation in our first season to the numerous unforgettable nights at St. James' Park in the Champions League soon after. The progression was fast.

'Everyone came together, united and what a force we became, culminating in bringing home our first domestic trophy in 70 years. These are all memories that I will cherish for the rest of my life.

'I would like to put on record my sincere thanks and appreciation to Yasir Al-Rumayyan, Jamie Reuben, Jacobo Solís and everyone at PIF, David Hopkinson, Ross Wilson and the entire ownership and leadership group for placing their trust in me and for giving me the opportunity to lead this special football club.

'I remain incredibly positive and enthusiastic about the future of Newcastle. The club is in fantastic hands with a great leadership team and I have no doubt together, alongside whoever comes in to replace me, they will continue to deliver success on the pitch.

'Thank you to Jason Tindall, Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches, Simon Weatherstone, Dan Hodges, Andy Howe and Jordan Tribe for their incredible loyalty, support and dedication and to all of the amazing staff behind the scenes whose hard work and loyalty makes this club what it is.

Howe steered Newcastle to Carabao Cup glory in 2025, ending their 70-year trophy drought

'A special thank you to all of the players who have represented the club during my time here. Without you, nothing would have been possible and it's been an honour to have coached you all.

'Finally, and most importantly, thank you to our incredible supporters. Your passion and loyalty have inspired me every single day. To stand on the touchline at St. James' Park as your manager with the honour of representing your club has meant more to me than you will ever know.

'While my journey as manager has now come to an end, the affinity and love I will always hold for Newcastle United never will.

'Thank you for everything. I wish the club every success for the future.'

The timing of Howe's departure has rocked Tyneside, even though it has not come as a surprise on the back of a turbulent 12 months.

After losing star striker Alexander Isak last September, England winger Anthony Gordon and Italy midfielder Sandro Tonali have been sold to Barcelona and Tottenham respectively this summer.

Arsenal have also today reached an agreement in principle to sign midfield leader Bruno Guimaraes for a fee that is understood to be worth £77million plus add-ons.

As revealed by Daily Mail Sport, Guimaraes dropped a bombshell on the Newcastle hierarchy several weeks ago by informing them of his desire to leave. And he did not fly with the rest of the Toon squad to their pre-season training camp in La Manga on Friday.

After arriving at St James' Park in November 2021, Howe accelerated Newcastle's status as a Premier League club by steering them to Champions League qualification on two occasions and ending their 70-year drought for a major domestic trophy.

David Hopkinson, Newcastle United's CEO, added: 'Eddie and his staff leave with the deep gratitude and respect of everyone at Newcastle United, and with a lasting place in the club's history.

Howe is being replaced by German coach Matthias Jaissle, who leaves Al-Ahli in Saudi Arabia

'While we are naturally disappointed to see Eddie leave, we remain immensely thankful for everything he has done for the club.

'On behalf of our owners, Board, players, staff and supporters, I would like to extend sincere thanks to Eddie for his outstanding service and leadership, and wish him and his family every success and happiness for the future.'

Sports.title: Mykhailo Mudryk is BACK: Chelsea outcast's doping nightmare is over as Blues and WADA agree to end four-year ban early - 20 months after he last played for West London club
Sports.content:
Mykhailo Mudryk is BACK: Chelsea outcast's doping nightmare is over as Blues and WADA agree to end four-year ban early - 20 months after he last played for West London club

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Mykhailo Mudryk’s doping ban has been lifted effective immediately with the Ukrainian now expected to join up with his Chelsea team-mates on their pre-season tour after being suspended for almost two years.

Mudryk, 25, was handed a four-year ban after being charged by the Football Association for failing a doping test, with his last appearance coming in November 2024 in the Conference League away at Heidenheim. He scored in that 2-0 win over their German opponents.

Yet it can now be confirmed that Mudryk will be allowed to return for the Premier League club – and sources at Chelsea have told Daily Mail Sport he is set to join up with his team-mates on their pre-season tour, most likely from their leg in Hong Kong after leaving Sydney this weekend.

It is a seismic resolution which has been struck after changes to the 'scientific reporting standards'.

Mudryk, who cost Chelsea £89million when they signed him from Shakhtar Donetsk in January 2023, posted on Instagram: 'After a long battle, the four-year ban that was imposed on me has been rescinded and I am free to resume my career with immediate effect.

'I am grateful that this process has reached a conclusion, that I have been cleared to return to football and that I can now look ahead to my future. This has been the most difficult period of my career.

Mykhailo Mudryk will return as Chelsea and WADA have agreed to end his four-year doping ban after 18 months

The winger pictured recently with his trainer as he prepares to take to the field again

'As I have always maintained from the outset of this case, I have never knowingly or intentionally taken any banned substance. My commitment to competing fairly and representing my club and country with professionalism and integrity has always been important to me.

'I would like to thank my family and friends for their support and belief throughout this period. I also want to express my deep gratitude to everyone at Chelsea FC, my teammates and the Chelsea supporters who have been with me throughout. I would also like to thank my legal team and others who assisted for their tireless work on my case.

'My focus now is on returning to football, working hard every day, and making a positive contribution on the pitch. Thank you to everyone who continued to believe in me. I look forward to the next chapter of my career.'

In a statement, Mudryk’s club said: ‘Chelsea FC acknowledges today's announcement by the Football Association confirming the resolution of the anti-doping proceedings involving Mykhailo Mudryk.

'From the outset, this has been an extremely difficult period for Misha, both professionally and personally, and we are pleased that the matter has now reached a conclusion which allows him to return to football with immediate effect.

‘We have always supported Misha throughout this process while fully respecting the integrity of the anti-doping system and the legal process.

‘We welcome the acknowledgement that advances in the applicable scientific reporting standards for more reliable testing mean that, had Misha's sample been analysed under today's technical requirements, it would not have been reported as a positive test and no anti-doping rule violation would have resulted.

'That is an important part of the context surrounding the agreed resolution and allows everyone involved to move forward.

‘Misha has consistently maintained that he never knowingly or intentionally used a prohibited substance and did not know how traces of the substance entered his system. Throughout this process he has conducted himself professionally and with resilience during what has undoubtedly been one of the most challenging periods of his career.

‘We know how much this opportunity to return means to him. Our focus now is on supporting Misha’s reintegration into the squad and helping him resume his career.

‘Chelsea FC remains fully committed to the highest standards of sporting integrity and compliance with all anti-doping regulations. Everyone at the club now looks forward to helping Misha return to full fitness, back into the squad and back onto the pitch.’

It is not yet known whether he will be staying with Chelsea for the 2026-27 season after so long without playing. Sources have confirmed the current plan is for him to join his team-mates on their pre-season, however. Xabi Alonso is due to speak next after their friendly versus Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday night, which kicks off at 7.45pm local time in Australia.

Mudryk has insisted from the very beginning that he never knowingly or intentionally took a prohibited substance. An important factor in the agreed resolution is the change made by the World Anti-Doping Agency to the scientific reporting standards used by accredited anti-doping laboratories when analysing samples for meldonium.

The laboratories use a qualitative testing method, meaning they estimate concentration levels rather than measure them precisely. Following developments in the scientific guidance, WADA increased the reporting threshold to provide greater confidence that samples reported as positive exceed the minimum reporting level.

In a statement, the FA revealed the entire timeline, explaining: ‘On October 22, 2024, Mr Mudryk was subject to an out-of-competition doping control, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance.

The FA notified Mr Mudryk of that finding on December 4, 2024 and imposed a provisional suspension. On May 23, 2025, the FA charged Mr Mudryk with ADRVs in breach of Regulations 3 and 4 of its 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

Mudryk has maintained his innocence throughout his ban and trained independently

The banned substance meldonium is believed to be behind the Ukrainian's failed test in 2024

‘On January 7 to 9, 2026, a hearing took place before an independent Regulatory Commission. The Regulatory Commission found that Mr Mudryk had committed the charged ADRVs and imposed a four-year period of ineligibility. Subsequently, Mr Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport. Since then, changes have been made to WADA Technical Document (TD2027MRL) which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no ADRVs would have resulted.

‘Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, the FA and Mr Mudryk have now – with the agreement of WADA – resolved the appeal proceedings in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the World Anti-Doping Code and Regulation 90 of the 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations. As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the Anti-Doping Rule Violations charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement.

He encouraged fans not to give up on him even when he had to train away from Chelsea

‘Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect.’

The precise source of the exposure has never been entirely identified. It is believed it occurred away from England while on international duty with Ukraine in September 2024.

Chelsea sources say they are grateful to both the FA and WADA for working constructively to reach a fair resolution in light of the updated scientific standards. The club's focus is now completely on supporting Mudryk’s return to football and helping him reintegrate into the squad.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's World Cup plot is unravelling as senior advisor QUITS and Asian Federation join leading nations in opposing controversial plan - denying deluded FIFA boss a majority
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's divisive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup appears to be dead after the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) joined UEFA and CONCACAF in opposing the plot - while two senior FIFA figures turned against him. Carlos Cordeiro, a retired American investment banker and senior adviser to Infantino, has resigned from his role at FIFA - becoming the first internal figure to do so. It comes after UEFA, CONCACAF and the AFC all opposed FIFA’s plans to generate £3.1billion in private investment in FIFA tournaments. 135 FIFA members are now publicly opposed to the FIFA Forward Enterprise, bringing the dissidents above the required 106 threshold to block the plans with dignitaries now joining the calls for Infantino to scrap his plans. Releasing a statement, Cordeiro - who served on the White House task force for the 2026 World Cup - distanced himself from Infantino’s plans and ripped into the proposals. Cordeiro urged his now former FIFA colleagues to follow suit and speak out against the plans, which he describes as a bad deal for football. Infantino had promised member associations a £30million incentive to force the deal through. 'As a Senior Advisor to the FIFA President, a former banker, and a lifelong football fan, I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup,’ Cordeiro said. 'Let me be clear: I had no involvement in this proposal, and I oppose it unequivocally. It is a bad deal for FIFA's Member Associations, a bad deal for football, and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game. 'It has been the privilege of a lifetime to serve FIFA for more than five years and to work alongside dedicated, principled people who care deeply about the game. I hope they, too, will speak up, because decisions of this magnitude should be made in the interests of football, not those who stand to profit from it.' FIFA’s chief operating officer Kevin Lamour responded to Cordeiro's call to action and publicly turned against Infantino. While Lamour stopped short of resigning as chief operating officer, a post he has held for two years, the Frenchman has put his job at risk by speaking out against FIFA’s chief. In a statement to the Associated Press, Lamour said: ‘It is the project of one person. Not only must this project not go ahead, but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions. ‘If that means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.’ Overnight, FIFA issued a statement, doubling down on plans to sell £3.1 billion in shares for FIFA tournaments after UEFA announced a boycott of competitions and CONCACAF - the North, Central, American and Caribbean federation - opposed the plans. But the AFC has now chosen to stand with their intercontinental counterparts, leaving Infantino's project - and potentially his FIFA presidency - facing a terminal threat. In a statement, the AFC said: 'The AFC stands in solidarity with UEFA and CONCACAF in expressing serious concerns over FIFA's proposal to introduce private investment into FIFA's flagship competitions and the decision-making process around FFE. 'The fact that the situation has reached the point where the real possibility of a FIFA World Cup boycott has entered public discourse should concern everyone who cares about the future of our game. Football should never have been placed in such a position. Gianni Infantino's controversial plan to sell off the World Cup appears to be dead in the water after the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) joined UEFA and CONCACAF in opposing the plot Infantino's senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro (right) has also now resigned in protest at the plans

Your browser does not support iframes.

'Against this backdrop, and in light of the clear positions expressed by UEFA and CONCACAF, as well as the unprecedented divisions that have emerged across the football world, the AFC believes that the proposed FFE cannot realistically achieve the necessary broad consensus and unity required to move forward. 'The FIFA World Cup is the pinnacle of global football and derives its strength from the participation of all Confederations and the world's leading football nations. 'Any proposal that risks undermining the unity and universal character of the competition must be reconsidered. 'While the immediate debate centres on FFE, the AFC considers this issue extends far beyond a single proposal. 'Rather, it has exposed fundamental weaknesses in FIFA's consultation and decision-making processes that must now be addressed. 'While the AFC notes FIFA's latest clarification on the proposal, the central concerns surrounding governance, institutional process and meaningful consultation remain unanswered. 'A proposal of such significance, with the potential to affect the commercial, sporting and strategic future of world football, must not emerge through processes that leave Confederations, Member Associations (MAs) and even FIFA's own governing bodies, including the FIFA Council, feeling sidelined. 'The primary objective for world football must be to ensure that decisions of such magnitude are being developed through processes that are anchored on transparency and command the confidence of the football community. 'This is not the first occasion where major stakeholders have been confronted with significant initiatives after the direction of travel appears to have already been determined. 'Such an approach undermines confidence in FIFA's governance framework and diminishes the authority of its statutory bodies. Join the discussion Should the World Cup ever be used as a tool for private profit, or does selling stakes betray the spirit of the game? FIFA issued a late-night response to furious backlash over the controversial plan to sell World Cup stakes to private investors by blaming the media for the uproar 'No subsequent consultation process, however well-intentioned, can replace early engagement with the appropriate FIFA bodies and the football family. 'The AFC believes this moment must become a catalyst for strengthening institutional reform. While every FIFA MA must have the opportunity to consider and determine proposals affecting the future of world football, meaningful democracy is not measured solely by the opportunity to vote. 'It begins with transparent governance, timely consultation, informed deliberation and genuine participation throughout the decision-making process. 'Accordingly, the AFC calls upon FIFA to undertake an urgent review of its governance and decision-making framework to ensure that proposals of global significance are developed through proper consultation, meaningful engagement and appropriate oversight by FIFA's statutory bodies. 'The FIFA World Cup, and the game itself, belong to the entire global football family. Their future must always be shaped collectively, through institutions that reflect the voices of all Confederations and MAs.' The AFC's statement criticises FIFA's clarification of their proposals released on Friday morning, where they blamed the media for misconstruing their plans and made a dig at UEFA for holding FIFA to account. FIFA said: 'We have heard the feedback provided by the respective confederations in relation to the proposed establishment of FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) and would like to address the issues that have surfaced since the initial media reporting on Tuesday. 'We respect the feedback and concern aired in public and reaffirm our commitment to an open and democratic consultation. ⁠'Our planned consultation process was disrupted by incorrect media reports. We will proceed with this consultation process to ensure that each MA has the ability to express its vote based on facts. 'FFE has been proposed solely to ensure that all FIFA Member Associations (MAs) have the opportunity to take meaningful ownership of the commercial opportunity of football in their respective countries, and that this does not come at the cost of either the spirit or the governance of FIFA or football itself. Infantino has been widely criticised for his decision to put the World Cup 'up for sale' The core investor would be a New York investment firm created by Joshua Kushner (pictured earliere this month in California), the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner 'Nobody is selling football. This is not something FIFA would ever entertain. 'Everyone has the right to express their opposition and to seek further clarification but no single entity can claim to represent all 211 MAs around the world. Each MA should be allowed to review the proposal and have a say in shaping their own future. These are the democratic principles of FIFA.' They continued by outlining the plans, subject to consultation with member nations. There is frustration across the international football landscape, however, that such proposals have been unilaterally developed - with proposed investors already lined up - in complete secrecy despite an eventual 'consultation'. UEFA nations are boycotting all FIFA competitions so long as the proposals remain on the table. All 55 UEFA nations met virtually on Thursday, with more than 40 federations providing testimony. Daily Mail Sport were told associations expressed ‘outrage’ on the call with ‘total unanimity’ against the proposal, before deciding to abstain from FIFA competitions. Daily Mail Sport also understands there is growing opposition to Infantino's presidency, with CONCACAF nations losing - or having already lost - confidence in the Swiss football administrator. UEFA and their member associations are yet to be drawn on that matter. Infantino is seeking a fourth term as FIFA president next year. One international football insider told Daily Mail Sport: ‘UEFA’s response is at the nuclear button end of the spectrum, which is impressive. We thought Infantino would survive the Trump refereeing intervention - but he has overreached this time.' In a statement, UEFA said: 'UEFA and its 55 member associations stand as one. We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA's proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors. 'The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football's greatest sporting legacies. It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale. 'It is both irresponsible and indefensible that a proposal of such significance for football was conceived in secret and brought to the brink of approval without any meaningful consultation with those entrusted with stewarding the game. This is not merely a profound failure of leadership, but an abdication of FIFA's duty as the custodian of world football. 'National associations around the world are now presented with an ultimatum: accept the irreversible capture of football's greatest competitions or bear the consequences. This is not a 'democratic decision', but governance by intimidation – an act of coercion unworthy of an institution entrusted with the stewardship of the global game. 'But our opposition goes far beyond process. 'The moment external investors acquire ownership interests in FIFA competitions, football changes forever. Commercial return becomes a permanent obligation. Investor expectations become a daily pressure. From that moment onwards, every decision on the international calendar, every decision on competition formats and every decision shaping the future of football is no longer driven by what best serves the game, but by what best serves shareholders. 'This model has no place in world football. Football's future cannot be dictated by the expectations of those whose first duty is to maximise financial return. Nor can the interests of national associations, leagues, clubs, players and supporters become subordinate to investor returns. Football cannot mortgage its future for financial gain. 'Europe's position is clear. We will never lend this model our legitimacy. No one has the moral authority to sell what they merely hold in trust for the next generation. 'As a result of today's discussion, no UEFA national teams will participate in any FIFA competition for so long as these proposals remain alive, unless this proposal has been abandoned in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that FIFA will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership. 'Nobody should be in any doubt: UEFA and its national associations will oppose these plans with absolute determination. 'There are moments when institutions are judged not by what they are prepared to accept, but by what they refuse to compromise. This is one of those moments. 'Some things are simply too important to sell. The FIFA World Cup belongs to football. It always will. And so long as Europe has a voice, it will never be for sale.’ An FA spokeswoman added: 'We stand shoulder to shoulder with our European colleagues and fully support the collective view. We oppose FIFA's plans - the FIFA World Cup belongs to football and always will.’ Concacaf later added: 'Concacaf is a confederation united by the love of our game, where football comes first. Guided by this philosophy over the past ten years we have built, from the ground up, an organisation founded on service, transparent governance, and the long-term stewardship of football. 'History has shown FIFA and the football family what happens when the custodians of the game lose sight of these values. 'With this in mind, Concacaf today convened a meeting of the presidents of its 41 Member Associations, together with its President, Council members, and its FIFA Council members, to discuss a proposal developed and presented by the FIFA President to establish 'FIFA Forward Enterprise' and sell interests in the FIFA World Cup to private investors. 'During the meeting, the membership expressed deep concerns about the lack of due process surrounding the proposal, the artificially short deadline imposed, and the absence of any review or approval by the relevant FIFA governance bodies. In addition, the need for private equity investment to fund new and existing FIFA Forward programs following the most profitable FIFA World Cup in history was questioned. 'The discussion reinforced the need for greater transparency and proper governance. 'For these reasons, Concacaf and its 41 Member Associations have: Rejected the proposal; Tasked their FIFA Council Members with engaging FIFA to determine how existing FIFA reserves could be used to increase FIFA Forward funding for football development across our region; and Tasked their FIFA Council Members with instructing the FIFA President to ensure that any matter follows the proper governance processes via staff and FIFA Council, in accordance with the FIFA Statutes. 'Through these actions, Concacaf reaffirms that football's future - and its greatest asset - must remain in the hands of our football family.'

Sports.title: Glorious Goodwood tips: Saturday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy
Sports.content:
Glorious Goodwood tips: Saturday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy

The Coral Stewards Cup is the highlight of the final day of Glorious Goodwood and Newsboy has provided detailed analysis of that and all the other races on Saturday

View 7 Images Newsboy provides tips for Goodwood (Image: PA)

1.50 Highclere Castle Gin Summer Handicap: VALEDICTORY has the going-places profile, not to mention the local knowledge, to bid his rivals ‘adieu’.

‌



The gelded son of Cracksman, trained in tandem by John and Thady Gosden, has taken his form to a new level since stepping up to a mile and three quarters and being equipped with cheekpieces.

‌



The combination worked a treat when Valedictory beat six opponents over course and distance at the end of May with a length-and-a-half beating of Spinning Wheel. And William Buick’s partner defied a 5lb rise in the weights at Newmarket’s July Festival 22 days ago, getting the better of Roaring Legend by a neck.

‌



Danny Mullins fined £2,500 for conduct near crowd on fractious Willie Mullins horse READ MORE :

Rising star jockey makes history by completing huge Galway Festival double READ MORE :

The latest intervention from the British Horseracing Authority number cruncher means Valedictory, with another 3lb on his back, competes from a mark of 95 today.

But the four-year-old is only just finding his feet and, with more to come, Valedictory has strong claims on the hat-trick. Align The Stars landed this race two years ago and the Northumberland Plate hero has to be respected, along with the Joseph O’Brien pair Aeronautic and Small Fry .

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 VALEDICTORY, 2 ALIGN THE STARS, 3 AERONAUTIC

‌



View 7 Images Al Aasy: fancied by Newsboy (Image: PA)

2.25 Coral Glorious Stakes: AL AASY is evergreen - and ripe for the Glorious Stakes hat-trick. At nine years of age, William Haggas’s stable stalwart is well into the veteran stage of his career but continues to be more than a match for younger legs.

His 12 victories from 30 outings - that’s an impressive 40% strike-rate - include eight triumphs in Group 3 company.

‌



In 2024, Al Aasy beat Relentless Voyager for this prize and he returned 12 months ago to defend his title with a three-length humbling of Meydan.

That effort was all the more meritorious when one considers he carried a 3lb penalty for his success in the same-level Gordon Richards Stakes at Sandown Park in the spring.

There is no such encumbrance today and a return to winning form in Beverley’s Listed Charlie Wood Stakes at the beginning of the month will set Tom Marquand’s mount up perfectly for today

‌



The biggest danger may come from fellow Somerville Lodge trainee Opportunity, with In My Teens and Enfjaar taken to fight it out for the bronze.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 AL AASY, 2 OPPORTUNITY, 3 IN MY TEENS

View 7 Images Willam Haggas: trains Santorini Star (Image: Photo by Alan Crowhurst/Getty Images)

‌



3.00 Qatar Lillie Langtry Stakes: SANTORINI STAR merits the chance to bounce back from a no-show at Royal Ascot last month.

Her challenge for the Group 2 Hardwicke Stakes on the final day of the fixture went badly awry as the William Haggas-saddled mare, a 16-1 chance, came home last of 12 behind Giavellotto.

But forgive that effort - Santorini Star was stepping back to a mile and a half and wearing cheekpieces that are dispensed with today - and the five-year-old daughter of Golden Horn is a definite player here.

‌



Having beaten Consent for the Group 2 Park Hill Fillies’ Stakes at Doncaster in September - the runner-up reversed the form in the top-level Prix de Royallieu at Longchamp next time - Santorini Star made a winning comeback under Tom Marquand against male opposition in the Group 2 Jockey Club Stakes at Newmarket in May.

And she ran another cracker when beaten a short neck by Caballo De Mar for the Group 1 Prix Vicomtesse Vigier over two miles at Longchamp 20 days later, before her Ascot flop.

Santorini Star, a course winner from her only previous visit to Goodwood, will be more at home back up in distance and shouldn’t be written off. Waardah and Danielle finished first and second 12 in this months ago, and should be in the firing line once more.

‌



View 7 Images Sondad: Newsboy's pick (Image: Niall Carson/PA Wire)

3.35 Coral Stewards' Cup: SONDAD has landed two big sprint-handicap pots this season, and a third could be on the way.

The fitting of a visor saw the Washington DC-sired gelding take one step forward after another for the father-and-son training combination of Mick and David Easterby in 2025.

‌



Having scored at Ascot in May of last year, Sondad followed up in a six-furlong event on Derby day at Epsom, finishing his campaign with podium efforts in competitive sprints won by Candy at Ayr (Ayr Silver Cup) and Aramram at Ascot.

And the five-year-old has continued his upward curve this term, stepping forward from a down-the-field effort behind Dark Thirty at York in May to retain his crown at Epsom the following month.

The draw gods didn’t play ball in the Wokingham Handicap at Royal Ascot a fortnight later - his berth in stall two could hardly have been worse - and, in the circumstance, a ninth behind Double Rush rates a commendable effort.

‌



But there were no such issues in another big-money affair on the Irish Oaks undercard at the Curragh last time, when Sondad and Easterby snr’s grand-daughter Jo Mason accounted for old rival Dark Thirty by half a length. He’s 1lb well in under a 6lb penalty and a draw in stall 21 should put Sondad in the thick of the action.

In a typically fiendish Stewards’ Cup, Far Above Dream, Annaf, Stratusnine and 2024 victor Get It are just four horses capable of getting involved.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 SONDAD, 2 FAR ABOVE DREAM, 3 GET IT

‌



View 7 Images Karl Burke: trains Newsboy's tip (Image: PA)

4.10 Phase Eight Handicap: NAVAL LIGHT and 3lb claimer Jack Nicholls are expected to prove a potent combination for the third time in a row.

The winner’s enclosure proved elusive for Havana Grey’s son on his first six visits to the racecourse. But, on the back of a sixth to Ten Carat Harry in a six-furlong handicap at Newmarket on 2,000 Guineas day, Naval Light, ridden by Nicholls for the first time, enjoyed a red-letter day when justifying odds of 2-5 in a maiden over the same trip at Pontefract 20 days later.

‌



Karl Burke then returned the gelded three-year-old to handicap company as Naval Light and Nicholls took on three rivals over seven furlongs at Catterick Bridge.

Sent off at 7-2, my selection swept through from the back of the field to lead inside the final furlong and account for Woodstock by a length and three-quarters.

Hot favourite Haaderr disappointed that day and more is need after a 5lb rise in the weights. But it will be a surprise if Naval Light can’t summon up another personal best and he’s fancied to go in again.

‌



We’re Goosers found the draw, and possibly the one-mile distance, against him in the Britannia Handicap at Royal Ascot and he heads the list of dangers, which also includes Ghost Mode and Ironwill.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 NAVAL LIGHT, 2 WE’RE GOOSERS, 3 IRONWILL

View 7 Images James Doyle: rides Newsboy's tip (Image: PA)

‌



4.45 British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes: MARKET LEADER did enough on his debut at Windsor, despite a defeat at odds-on, to be of interest here.

Punters were falling over themselves to back the 450,000-Euro breeze-up purchase when he took on eight opponents for a six-furlong novice stakes at Windsor 19 days ago - Market Leader went off the 4-5 hotpot.

But they were soon biting their nails when James Doyle’s partner made a sluggish exit from the starting stalls and trailed the field during the early exchanges.

‌



Market Leader then appeared nonplussed when his jockey urged him forwards inside the final quarter mile but did learn on the job in coming home in third, four lengths behind winner Real Bullet.

Given his obvious lack of streetwisdom, Market Leader, who holds an entry in the Group 1 Vincent O’Brien National Stakes at the Curragh next month, looks capable of a big step forward, and the seventh furlong should help.Regency Royal, Speakers Corner and Leadlight all performed with promise first time up and should improve

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 MARKET LEADER, 2 REGENCY ROYAL, 3 SPEAKERS CORNER

‌



View 7 Images Clive Cox trains Newsboy pick (Image: PA)

5.20 Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap: BLUE COURVOISIER, another horse who missed out on the luck of the draw at Royal Ascot, makes plenty of appeal under Saffie Osborne.

The debut winner of a Leicester novice stakes on his first of two outings as a two-year-old in 2025, the son of Sea The Stars made the frame in handicaps at Newmarket and Ascot when returning in the spring.

‌



With Osborne on board for the first time, Blue Courvoisier gave his trainer Clive Cox a third Silver Bowl triumph when holding Langstone by a length and a half at Carlisle - the one-mile handicap was switched from Haydock Park - at the end of May.

Blue Courvoisier couldn’t get involved from stall one when 18th of 30 in the Britannia Handicap but shouldn’t be written off.

In a wide-open meeting finale, Crest Of Fire, El Matador, Boyfriend and Great Chieftain are names to throw into the mix.

Article continues below

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 BLUE COURVOISIER, 2 CREST OF FIRE, 3 BOYFRIEND

Sports.title: Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Saturday on ITV
Sports.content:
Value Scope: Each way horseracing tips from Steve Jones for Saturday on ITV

On the final day of Glorious Goodwood, there is one outstanding betting race, the Coral Stewards' Cup and our man thinks he has the answer to the tricky sprint

View Image Steve Jones with his picks for Glorious Goodwood on ITV

It's not hard to be a Fan of the Coral Stewards’ Cup. With more than two dozen sprinters hurtling across the beautiful South Downs on the final day of Glorious Goodwood, it is one of the most stunning sights in Flat racing.

‌



Having started with Wesley Ward in America, he went on to have a spell in Ireland with Joseph O’Brien before twice running on the ice at St Moritz for Olly Murphy.

‌

Sports.title: Matthias Jaissle can hand Newcastle chance to sign title winner and help fill Anthony Gordon void
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle can hand Newcastle chance to sign title winner and help fill Anthony Gordon void

Newcastle United look to be closing in on appointing Matthias Jaissle as the replacement for Eddie Howe.

View 2 Images Newcastle United look set to appoint Matthias Jaissle as their new head coach. (Image: Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images))

It’s set to be all change for Newcastle United this summer, both in the dugout and on the pitch. After five years in charge of the club, Eddie Howe has left St James’ Park.

‌



The news broke just a matter of hours after the 4-1 friendly defeat against Championship side Bristol City. It seems to be a time of Chaos for Newcastle.

‌



The manager is said to have made the decision, which follows the sales of Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon earlier this summer. Gordon moved to Barcelona for a fee of £69.3 million, with Tonali completing a £100 million transfer to Tottenham.

‌



The Premier League special edition is on sale now READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes pushes for Arsenal transfer with Newcastle agreement imminent READ MORE :

There is also speculation over the futures of both Bruno Guimaraes and Lewis Hall. Arsenal are being strongly linked with Guimaraes , and Manchester United interested in Hall.

For Newcastle, the focus will be on bringing in replacements for Howe and handling any outgoings between now and the Premier League opener. The Magpies seem to be closing in on a deal for Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle.

If that appointment is made, then it could potentially open up the door for Newcastle to move for a former Premier League title winner, who could help to fill some of the void of the quality left by the sales.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

While at Al-Ahil, Jaissle has worked closely with Riyad Mahrez. Under the German coach, he played 122 games, scoring 37 times and providing 50 assists.

The 35-year-old officially left the club this summer and is now available on a free transfer. He could be a player who Jaissle could turn to as he looks to make an impact at Newcastle.

‌



Mahrez’s age and the fact that he has been playing in Saudi Arabia means that he may not be expected to start every game. Newcastle have already brought in a replacement for Gordon in Bazoumana Toure.

View 2 Images Riyad Mahrez is available on a free transfer this summer. (Image: Ercin Erturk/Anadolu via Getty Images)

But, Mahrez, who has won five Premier League titles with Leicester City and Manchester City, would no doubt add some Premier League know-how and quality to Newcastle’s squad.

‌



Speaking about his relationship with Mahrez in December 2024, Jaissle told RMC Sport: "Mahrez is a fantastic footballer, I have a very good relationship with him. And I think if you ask him, he'll probably tell you the same thing.

“I can only say that I'm really happy to have him on the team. He's an incredible player, he's won everything. And he's showing it again this year with the difference he's able to make during matches.”

Mahrez captained Algeria in this summer’s World Cup, scoring twice and providing an assist in his four appearances in the competition. He announced his retirement from international football following the tournament, meaning he’ll be concentrating on his club career.

Article continues below

Fabrizio Romano reports that he is keen to return to Europe, with Serie A Clubs showing an interest. Despite his age, having the chance to sign someone of Mahrez’s quality may be one that Newcastle shouldn’t turn down.

Sports.title: Newcastle United confirm Eddie Howe exit with statement issued as replacement lined up
Sports.content:
Newcastle United confirm Eddie Howe exit with statement issued as replacement lined up

Eddie Howe ended Newcastle United's barren run without a major trophy but will now depart the club after nearly five years of service

View 2 Images Eddie Howe has walked away from his role as Newcastle United boss (Image: MI News/NurPhoto)

Newcastle United have confirmed Eddie Howe has resigned from his position as manager. Earlier reports had stated the Englishman was set to walk away from the club after nearly five years at the helm.

‌



He was the first permanent manager to be appointed by the club after the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund's takeover toward the end of 2021. The ex-Bournemouth manager guided the Magpies into the Champions League on two occasions and won the League Cup to end their 70-year wait without a trophy.

‌



However, things grew more difficult for Howe when Alexander Isak joined Liverpool for £125million and while around £240m was spent on new signings, the club struggled to a 12th placed Premier League finish. After seeing Anthony Gordon join Barcelona, Sandro Tonali join Tottenham Hotspur for £100m and Bruno Guimaraes inform the club he also wants to depart, Howe's resignation has been confirmed.

‌



Newcastle confirmed the news in a statement, which read: "Newcastle United can announce that Eddie Howe has informed the club of his decision to step down as head coach.

Bruno Guimaraes pushes for Arsenal transfer with Newcastle agreement imminent READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes given separate Newcastle plan as showdown transfer talks scheduled READ MORE :

"The club has accepted Eddie’s decision and would like to thank him for his extraordinary contribution.

"Also leaving the club are coaches Jason Tindall, Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches and Simon Weatherstone, and head of performance Dan Hodges."

‌



Howe went on to issue an emotional farewell message to Newcastle fans, with the 48-year-old saying: “After a period of personal reflection, I have decided that now is the right time for me to step away from my role as head coach of Newcastle United.

“After nearly five years of giving my life, heart and soul into the club with unrelenting energy, I feel that it is in the best interests of both myself and the club to step away, recharge and take a break.

“Although it’s been incredibly difficult to make this decision, I know in my heart that it’s the right one. I have always put the best interests of Newcastle before my own in every single decision I have made whilst I’ve been here and this one is no different.

‌



“It has been the privilege of my lifetime to have been the manager of Newcastle United.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“It is difficult to put into words what this club, the city and its supporters mean, and will always mean, to me and my family. From the moment myself, Jason and all of the staff arrived nearly half a decade ago, Newcastle instantly felt like home and the people here welcomed us with open arms. We took huge pride in representing the club from day one and this city will always hold a very special place in our hearts.

‌



“There have been so many incredible moments in our time here. From fighting relegation in our first season to the numerous unforgettable nights at St. James’ Park in the Champions League soon after. The progression was fast.

“Everyone came together, united and what a force we became, culminating in bringing home our first domestic trophy in 70 years. These are all memories that I will cherish for the rest of my life.

“I would like to put on record my sincere thanks and appreciation to Yasir Al-Rumayyan, Jamie Reuben, Jacobo Solís and everyone at PIF, David Hopkinson, Ross Wilson and the entire ownership and leadership group for placing their trust in me and for giving me the opportunity to lead this special football club.

‌



“I remain incredibly positive and enthusiastic about the future of Newcastle. The club is in fantastic hands with a great leadership team and I have no doubt together, alongside whoever comes in to replace me, they will continue to deliver success on the pitch.

View 2 Images Eddie Howe has officially left Newcastle United (Image: David Davies/PA Wire)

“Thank you to Jason Tindall, Graeme Jones, Stephen Purches, Simon Weatherstone, Dan Hodges, Andy Howe and Jordan Tribe for their incredible loyalty, support and dedication and to all of the amazing staff behind the scenes whose hard work and loyalty makes this club what it is.

‌



“A special thank you to all of the players who have represented the club during my time here. Without you, nothing would have been possible and it’s been an honour to have coached you all.

“Finally, and most importantly, thank you to our incredible supporters. Your passion and loyalty have inspired me every single day. To stand on the touchline at St. James’ Park as your manager with the honour of representing your club has meant more to me than you will ever know.

“While my journey as manager has now come to an end, the affinity and love I will always hold for Newcastle United never will.

‌



“Thank you for everything. I wish the club every success for the future.”

Matthias Jaissle, 38, is expected to become the next Newcastle manager having previously coached Saudi Arabian side Al-Ahli, who he guided to two Asian Cup titles, the continent's version of the Champions League.

Sports.title: Bookies ‘run out of cash’ at Wolverhampton after favourite lands £50,000 gamble
Sports.content:
Bookies ‘run out of cash’ at Wolverhampton after favourite lands £50,000 gamble

The victory of 2-1 chance Iconic Times, trained by Jennie Candlish, was claimed to have cost racecourse bookmakers £50,000 when winning at the all-weather meeting

View 2 Images Bookmakers allegedly ran out of cash at Wolverhampton (Image: wolverhampton-racecourse.co.uk)

Bookmakers ‘ran out of cash’ at Wolverhampton on Thursday night after a heavily backed favourite landed a monumental gamble. Division one of the Download the Raceday Ready App Handicap was a lowly Class 6 race over 7f contested by 12 runners.

‌



But punters at the track only wanted to back one horse, the Jennie Candlish-trained Iconic Times. In four runs since joining the stable his nearest finish had been sixth over a mile at Southwell in April. He had finished tenth on his previous start when he went off a 28-1 chance.

‌



This time he opened at odds of 3-1 and was returned the 2-1 favourite after hitting the front a furlong out and running out the length winner. Local layer Barry Pinnington, who trades as Pinno, was reporting updates from the track on social media.

‌



Danny Mullins fined £2,500 for conduct near crowd on fractious Willie Mullins horse READ MORE :

Rising star jockey makes history by completing huge Galway Festival double READ MORE :

His first post said: “Massive gamble on course here @WolvesRaces. Fortunes for Iconic Times 25k plus.”

After the race he said: “8 books in the ring, I paid out 8k, others paid out a lot more.”

He added: “First bet in my book was a 1000 at 7/1. My colleagues were laying thousands at 5/2 just before the off. I’m amazed there were enough readies in the ring to pay out

‌



“Such a shame there is no proper betting or show reports from the ring these days. The post reports that on the 7th race at Wolves the winner opened 3/1 touched 10/3 returned 2/1. The truth is it opened 7/1 on the track and good money was laid. Bring back the on course reporters.”

View 2 Images Jennie Candlish: trainer of Iconic Times (Image: RACINGFOTOS.COM)

John Hutchinson from BDC Racing told the Racing Post, "It was a monumental gamble and quite an expensive night.

‌



"Never before have I seen every bookmaker run out of cash on a racecourse, but they did last night. That's how bad it was."

The stewards held an inquiry into the winner who “appeared to show improved form compared with its previous run at Wolverhampton on 1 June 2026 where the gelding finished tenth of 12 runners, beaten by 7 lengths.”

The report said: “Jennie Candlish’s representative’s explanation that ICONIC TIMES had benefitted from the reapplication of cheekpieces, was noted. The gelding was routine tested.”

Sports.title: Chelsea star Mykhailo Mudryk shares emotional message after doping ban lifted
Sports.content:
Chelsea star Mykhailo Mudryk shares emotional message after doping ban lifted

Mykhailo Mudryk has had his suspension from football lifted and been given the green light to return to playing, with the Chelsea winger poised to join the club's pre-season tour in Hong Kong.

View 2 Images Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk has been given the green light to return to football (Image: PA Wire)

Mykhailo Mudryk has broken his silence after being given the green light to return to football, with the FA confirming disciplinary proceedings against the Chelsea star have now been resolved. The 25-year-old winger is now poised to link up with the Blues on their pre-season tour in Hong Kong.

‌



Mudryk last featured for the club since November 2024. The Ukrainian international was given a four-year suspension by the FA following an anti-doping violation after testing positive for meldonium, but the player appealed the decision to the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

‌



Writing on Instagram, Mudryk said: "After a long battle, the four-year ban that was imposed on me has been rescinded, and I am free to resume my career with immediate effect. I am grateful that this process has reached a conclusion, that I have been cleared to return to football and that I can now look ahead to my future.

‌



"This has been the most difficult period of my career. As I have always maintained from the outset of this case, I have never knowingly or intentionally taken any banned substance.

Mykhailo Mudryk ban LIFTED as FA release statement confirming Chelsea star can play again READ MORE :

How Chelsea managed to escape Premier League points deduction as FA explain charges READ MORE :

"My commitment to competing fairly and representing my club and country with professionalism and integrity has always been important to me. I would like to thank my family and friends for their support and belief throughout this period.

"I also want to express my deep gratitude to everyone at Chelsea FC, my teammates and the Chelsea supporters who have been with me throughout. I would also like to thank my legal team and others who assisted for their tireless work on my case.

‌



"My focus now is on returning to football, working hard every day, and making a positive contribution on the pitch. Thank you to everyone who continued to believe in me. I look forward to the next chapter of my career."

View 2 Images Mykhailo Mudryk has not played since 2024 (Image: Danehouse Photography Ltd/Getty Images)

A statement from the FA explained the lifting of Mudryk's ban, which read: "The FA can confirm that the anti-doping disciplinary proceedings against Mykhailo Mudryk were resolved with the agreement of the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) on 30 July 2026. In the context of that agreement, Mr Mudryk has accepted his commission of Anti-Doping Rule Violations (ADRVs) and accepted a period of ineligibility.

‌



"On 22 October 2024, Mr Mudryk was subject to an out-of-competition doping control, which revealed the presence of a low concentration of meldonium, a prohibited substance. The FA notified Mr Mudryk of that finding on 4 December 2024 and imposed a provisional suspension. On 23 May 2025, The FA charged Mr Mudryk with ADRVs in breach of Regulations 3 and 4 of its 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations. "On 7 to 9 January 2026, a hearing took place before an independent Regulatory Commission. The Regulatory Commission found that Mr Mudryk had committed the charged ADRVs and imposed a four-year period of ineligibility. Subsequently, Mr Mudryk filed an appeal with the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"Since then, changes have been made to WADA Technical Document (TD2027MRL) which, while not retroactive, mean that if Mr Mudryk's sample was collected today, the concentration of meldonium in the sample would not have been reported and no ADRVs would have resulted. "Further to that development and to other circumstances of the case, The FA and Mr Mudryk have now - with the agreement of WADA - resolved the appeal proceedings in accordance with Article 10.8.2 of the World Anti-Doping Code and Regulation 90 of the 2024 Anti-Doping Regulations.

Article continues below

"As a part of the agreement, Mr Mudryk accepted that he had committed the Anti-Doping Rule Violations charged and acceded to a period of ineligibility equal to the time served at the date of the agreement. Mr Mudryk is no longer ineligible and may return to competition with immediate effect."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
